newsitem.title: CANADA: CWB says West Coast railcar unloads below targets.
newsitem.headline: CWB says West Coast railcar unloads below targets.

text.p: The number of hopper cars carrying grains and oilseeds from Canada's Prairies to export position on the Pacific Coast fell well below assigned targets in the week ended February 9, a Canadian Wheat Board spokeswoman said.
There were 1,994 railcars unloaded at Vancouver compared to the alloted 3,000 cars, CWB spokeswoman Rhea Yates said.
Unloads at Prince Rupert totalled 1,160 compared to the alloted 1,300, Yates added.
The CWB faces more than C$15 million in demurrage fees on ships piled up on Canada's Pacific Coast since early January.

Canadian Agriculture Minister Ralph Goodale plans to speak early this week with shippers Canadian National Railway Co and Canadian Pacific unit CP Rail System as well as the CWB to try to expedite shipments, Goodale's spokesman Vern Greenshields said.
There were 38 ships waiting to load grains and oilseeds at Canada's Pacific ports as of last Friday. The longest waiting vessel had been in port for 36 days.
